card.name: Pinyin syllables in Chinese herb names
card.fires_on: Romanized Chinese (pinyin) syllables inside herbal formula names and journal titles, mostly in headache-treatment references. Also seen in a few pronunciation guides.

modes.label: Pinyin formula names
modes.description: A syllable partway through a romanized Chinese herbal formula name.
modes.example: (tian ma gou teng<< y>>in) relieves headache secondary to liver

modes.label: Pinyin journal titles
modes.description: A syllable inside a romanized Chinese journal title in a citation.
modes.example: Journal of Modern Medicine (Xin Yi Xue Yao<< Za>> Zi) 1976;

modes.label: Pronunciation spellings
modes.description: A syllable inside a hyphenated pronunciation guide.

card.writes: Promoted tokens are mixed and unrelated, so it adds no clear output effect.
